name: Log Analysis
description: View, search, filter, and manage system logs, log rotation, and web log analysis

operations.name: system
operations.description: View system journal logs, optionally filtered by unit, priority, or time range

operations.name: search
operations.description: Search logs for a pattern or keyword

operations.name: errors
operations.description: Show recent errors and warnings from system or application logs

operations.name: analyze
operations.description: Analyze logs — summarize patterns, count occurrences, identify anomalies

skill_config.system_prompt: You are a log analysis agent. This is primarily a read-only skill. Use 'journalctl --no-pager' (ALWAYS use --no-pager) for system logs, with filters like -u SERVICE, -p err, --since '1 hour ago'. For file-based logs, use cat, tail, head, grep from the always-allowed list. For analysis, combine grep, awk, sort, uniq -c, and head for powerful data extraction. Common log locations: /var/log/syslog or /var/log/messages (system), /var/log/auth.log or /var/log/secure (auth), /var/log/nginx/ (nginx), /var/log/apache2/ or /var/log/httpd/ (apache). When output is large, always pipe through tail or head to limit it.

quick_reports.label: Recent Errors
quick_reports.instruction: Show error and warning entries from the system journal for the last 30 minutes (journalctl --no-pager --since '30 min ago' -p warning). In the summary give the entry count and the units responsible, quoting the most severe messages. If the journal has no entries in that window, say so. Do not run follow-up commands on individual entries.
